definitions.text: Three or more than three-sided closed figure is called polygon.
Similar figures have same shape but not necessarily of same size.

Two polygons are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and the corresponding sides are proportional (i.e., the ratios of the lengths of corresponding sides are equal). This means that if two polygons are similar, one is a scaled version of the other.
Proportionality of sides means one side is k times of its corresponding side.

If two angles in one triangle are congruent to two corresponding angles in another triangle, the third angle in each triangle must be congruent. Since the angles are the same, the triangles are similar. Similarity symbol is ‘~’.
If the ratio of two corresponding sides and their included angle are equal, then the triangles are similar.
If the ratio of all the corresponding sides are equal, then the triangles are similar.
Hence the ratio of the areas of any two similar figures is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding lengths of the figures.
Since each length is k times of the other, we take ℓ₁/ℓ₂ = k, then A₁/A₂ = k². i.e. Area A₁ is k² times the area A₂. k is called scale factor.

Two solids are said to be similar if they have same shape but possibly different sizes. Two solids are similar if lengths of the corresponding sides are proportional i.e., the ratio of the corresponding lengths are equal.
Hence the ratio of the volume of any two similar solids is equal to the cube of the ratio of any two corresponding lengths of the solids.
Since mass of a substance is proportional to its volume, the ratio of the mass of two similar solids is equal of to the ratio of their volumes.

fullMarks: Start a similarity proof by naming the two figures and matching their corresponding vertices in the correct order, such as ΔABC ~ ΔDEF.
For a triangle similarity proof, show the matching angles or write all three corresponding side ratios and show that they are equal.
Keep the order of corresponding figures consistent in every ratio; do not compare a side with a non-corresponding side.
For area questions, write A₁/A₂ = (ℓ₁/ℓ₂)² before substituting values. For volume questions, write V₁/V₂ = (ℓ₁/ℓ₂)³.
If an area ratio is given and a length is required, take the square root of the area ratio. If a volume ratio is given and a length is required, take the cube root.
Show the proportion, substitution and rearrangement as separate steps, then write the final answer clearly.
Include the correct units in the final answer: cm² or m² for area, and cm³ or m³ for volume.
mistakes: Using the length ratio directly as the area ratio. Fix: square the corresponding-length ratio.
Using the square of the length ratio for volumes. Fix: cube the corresponding-length ratio.
Reversing one ratio but not the others. Fix: keep the same figure first in every numerator and the other figure in every denominator.
Taking a square root when finding a length from a volume ratio. Fix: take the cube root for volumes.
Matching sides in the wrong order when writing a triangle similarity statement. Fix: list the corresponding vertices in the same order before forming ratios.
Leaving off square or cubic units. Fix: write units such as cm² for area and cm³ for volume in the final answer.
